question: How does a conventional first-order Markov model compare on the exact earlier known-slot queries?
outcome: Markov top-one 34.5861%, PMB 33.8120%, PM 16.9934% on the same 8,009 masks. PMB minus Markov top-one interval includes zero; Markov top-five and bucket log loss improve. This is the conceptual Markov family with unigram-prior smoothing, distinct from the published modified Kneser–Ney estimator.
challenge: A stronger conventional comparator had to retain the existing query identities, grouping, folds and training-only selection.
remedy: Exact correspondence checks, nested smoothing selection, paired component intervals and independent recalculation of every query prediction.
retry_when: A declared new estimator, independently tuned start distribution or changed observation population supplies a distinct comparison. Reuse saved masks and predictions.

question: Which learned boundaries and interior transitions support restoration?
outcome: Removing only the end factor lowers final-slot top-one from 53.95% to 48.25%. Interior-only training shuffles average 24.52% overall versus 34.59% full Markov; all-slot shuffles average 14.88%. Unigram start replacement lowers initial top-one while improving initial bucket loss. Rare-target calibration remains poor despite low overall calibration error.
challenge: Deleting an inference factor and refitting without end events have different effects. Training transformations can incidentally recreate held-out texts.
remedy: Separate interventions, fixed original groups and smoothing, twenty saved training orders per control, logged accidental text coincidences and independent prediction checks.
retry_when: A training-only start-shrinkage or historical transition estimator changes the comparison; retain all existing mechanism endpoints.

question: Which physical-use and chronological comparisons can the preserved corpus support?
outcome: Informative depth appears in 2,810/5,680 rows; an earlier rule counted 2,870 placeholder strings as present. Metadata repeats across object faces. Three Harappa physical-use groups contain 69 source objects, 60 joined objects and only two objects in the main >=3-sign population. All 66 faces of 22 copied tablets are complete two-sign observations.
challenge: Placeholders, duplicated object metadata, site-dependent chronological labels and ambiguous identifier punctuation change apparent coverage.
remedy: Row/family counts, explicit placeholder and interval categories, full source introduction acquisition, separately frozen cohort/identifier refinements and source-coordinate checks.
retry_when: Object plates/basic-data tables resolve identifiers or new independently dated/attached-object observations support a defined comparison.

question: Can integrated reference uncertainty and further-record prediction diagnose confident wrong maps?
outcome: The 2,592-trial grid spans 24 new systems and 216 conditions. Integrated reference uncertainty removes confident wrong cases in the unchanged administrative conditions but leaves failures after a process change. Erroneous supplied identities usually worsen held-out score, with saved exceptions under the constrained model.
challenge: Finite reference parameters, a mismatched stationary model and a wrong supplied identity contribute different failures. Archived source-path imports initially sought the helper under the wrong directory.
remedy: Dirichlet-integrated ordered-sequence scores, exact mapping enumeration, paired held-out populations, separate identity conditions, frozen-byte execution with original path context and independent scalar/sequential scores for all 216 conditions.
retry_when: A new observation-selection, variable-inventory, segmentation or physically grounded identity model changes the supplied benchmark assumptions.
